259	## 2. For the curator
260	
261	### The words this record uses
262	
263	- **Walk** is the interpreter. The **compiled path** checks a program's types with the **checker**, then makes JVM bytecode with the **code generator**, and runs it on the compiled **run time**. Until the **switch-over**, the compiled path uses its own small library, the **prelude**. After it, the compiled path uses the interpreter's library, the **one library**.
264	- A **native binding** is a library declaration whose body is `builtinPrimitive("…")`. Its string names a **glue class**, which only walk can call, or a **helper**, a static Java method in `nativeHelpers/`, which both paths call (P-58). A **carrier** is the Java type in which walk passes a declared type to a helper. **P-167's device**: the binding names a compiled helper, and walk's loader answers that name with walk's own glue, as for `ilkName` and `SEQV`; P-169 makes it the rule for the run time's own operations.
265	- A **Java-backed trait** is a trait of the one library whose values a Java class holds, as `JavaBufferedWriter` holds a Java writer: walk's private native object below it, and the compiled run-time class that implements it (P-164).
266	- **The count** and **the distance** are the checker's errors on the one library: the count on its main component, the distance on its fourteen core components. Both are 0 at the last gate, and the distance has two **crash rows**, where the checker stopped inside `value object Char` (F-53, F-54; row 929).
267	- The compiled **transaction** is the compiled run time's software transactional memory, which a compiled `atomic` block starts and ends; it tracks each mutable **cell** that the block reads or writes. **Decision A** is the array decision that gives an `RR64` array an unboxed `double[]` store (P-84).
268	- A **rung** is one change, built by one worker and checked by a second agent, the skeptic. A **batch** is a few rungs landed together after the **gate**. The **gather** composes the rungs on `main`. A **guard** is a test that passes before the change and after it.
269	- **Appendix I** is the specification's appendix of changes. A revised passage carries a **callout** that names its entry there.
270	- **microGPT** is the model program, by which the revival is measured. A **model line** is a source line of either of its programs; no rung of this batch changes one.

35:## The go
36-
37-- The batches of PLAN's phase 3 run on a standing go, in PLAN's order. Launch each when the batch before it has landed and its own batch record has no open question.
38-- Put into a batch record every piece of work on PLAN's road that moves the project forward and is well defined: its decisions are taken. A new deliverable still waits for its go (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions"). A piece that is not well defined waits. A well-defined piece waits only if it would put the batch's merge at risk. Two rungs put it at risk if the gather cannot merge their edits of one file or one declaration cleanly. A pair that merges cleanly but changes one behaviour two ways, or where one needs the other's result, goes in one batch only if one lands only with the other (the manifest's `landsOnlyWith`).
39-- If a question that the batch record raises is consequential (`SKILL.md`), put it to the curator first. Otherwise decide it and put it on the review list. While the curator is away, overnight, take its recommended default and put it on the review list. If that default would reverse a decision of the curator, hold that batch, and launch the repair batch (`explorations/coordinator/REPAIR-BATCH.md`) in its place.
40-- Have one Fable review read each coming batch record before the launch, with a go in advance. It is written for the curator in place of reading the record. Treat its questions as the batch record's.

43-
44-- Between batches, improve the script and the manual where a batch showed a problem.
45-- Let every step spend the fewest workers that it needs.
46-- Build the base once, yourself, in a worktree where nobody compiles or runs (`args.baseBuild`). Every rung worktree is seeded from it (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`), never built clean.
47-- No stage runs a build, a suite or a measurement again on a code state that another stage ran, and no agent reads again a log that has not changed.

93-The revival resolves the contradictions that the team left, by the evidence in the repository: the specification, the papers, the library and the code. The curator does not redesign the language, and decides a contradiction that the evidence leaves open, by the designers' intent. The curator's words show what the curator decided. They are not the ground of the design.
94-
95:Three principles settle most forks: the team's later word (P-26), the library as the team wrote it, and what peer languages do. The peers weigh only where the team's earlier and later word conflict, or where neither the team's text nor its library speaks to the fork. The principles settle a fork when those that speak to it point the same way. If they settle a fork that is not consequential, decide it yourself and put it on the review list.
96-
97-Weigh a team text by its provenance: who wrote it, in which role, such as a core designer or an outside contributor of the open-source years, and whether the team reviewed it or its author called it provisional. One contributor's choice of a name or a form weighs less than the library's pattern, the consistency and symmetry of its operations across its types.
98-
99:A decision is consequential if it:
100-
101-- reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of the curator's;
102-- touches microGPT: a line of its two programs, its speed or its readability;
103-- chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent;
104-- or cannot be undone.
105-
106-It reaches the curator in one of three ways:
107-
108-1. **Asked before the work.** A known fork is probed, and put as an ask before the batch is briefed.
109-2. **Landed, then reviewed.** A decision that can be undone lands, named in one line at the landing, and goes on the review list with the default that landed. Put it to the curator later, one per message.
--
114-- Launch a probe or an Opus worker without asking. Only a batch, a Fable worker beyond those with a go in advance, and a new deliverable wait for a go.
115-- Launch a batch only on the curator's explicit go. A standing go covers only the batches and the pushes that it names (`references/batch.md`).
116-- Before you ask the curator anything, or measure anything, search the record (below). If it settles the question, act on it. An entry's history is part of that search, and is read before any claim about the entry's reasons, since the history keeps the ground and the curator's words that the entry's text leaves out.
117:- If a decision that a worker wrote in one line of its report is consequential, it is not made until the curator sees it. Bring it by one of the three ways.
118-- A worker that looks for issues gives all its findings the same weight. Sort the findings yourself, by what each needs, before any finding reaches the curator or goes into the next brief:
119-  - If a finding would change a decision of the curator's, put it to the curator as an ask. No other finding becomes an ask.
120-  - If a reason in the record is no longer true, cut it. You need no approval to bring the record in line with reality.
121-  - If a finding corrects the ground of an entry and changes no decision, put it in the entry's history. It changes nothing that a reader does.
122-  - If a finding confirms a decision, give it one line.
123-- Keep a proposal of yours marked as yours until the curator says yes.
124-- Act on a side remark within the work that may start, but record no decision from it. Write a one-time go nowhere: the launch or the commit is its trace.
125:- When something goes wrong or is undecided, find the cause and choose the best way forward for the whole. If that choice is consequential, bring it by one of the three ways. Do not roll back or bisect.
126-- Weigh a rule by what it protects against what it costs. If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix. Propose one too when a file grows or a rule makes clutter.
127-- Have the skill writer add, change or remove a rule of this skill, in `SKILL.md` or in a part, only after a cold read of the change (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"). A fix of a path or a section name is a change too, except at an approved draft's landing (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). The writer's fixes of the cold read's flags land with no second cold read. Then the change lands without the curator's yes, also when you proposed it, unless the bullet after next says that it waits. A line of `references/sources.md` is not a rule, and needs neither a cold read nor a report.
128-- After a change to this skill or to `fortress-repo` lands, have a worker update that skill's page: the page of skill drafts or the page of `fortress-repo` changes, whose links the boot note holds (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). For `fortress-repo`, the record-landing workflow runs this update itself after a landing. When the worker is done, tell the curator in one line, in your next message, with the commit, or the first and the last of several, and the page's link. Watch both pages for comments sent to Claude. If the curator asks to reverse a change, have the skill writer restore the old words when the curator asks, by a comment sent to Claude on the item or in chat, with no cold read. The reversal does not wait for the end of the curator's reading. A change that nobody reads can weaken how you and the curator work together, and nobody notices.
129-- A change that touches the curator's role and decisions (this section), the asks, the held list, the review list or the register in which you write to the curator (the bullets at the head of "Talking to the curator") waits for the curator's yes to its exact words. So does every rewrite of this skill's `SKILL.md` or of a whole part of this skill, since it can touch any rule. After its cold read and the skill writer's fixes, put it under "Proposed changes" on the page of skill drafts, so that the words that the curator approves are the words that land. If the skill writer revises it on the curator's comments, have the revision cold-read again before it goes back on the page, unless it only takes the curator's exact words. Such a change has no default: it stays out of the skill until the yes. If you are unsure whether a change touches these, it waits.
130-- Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`. No change of them waits for the curator's yes, a change of their `SKILL.md` or a new rule included. Each lands after its cold read and the skill writer's fixes. For `fortress-repo`, the bullet above on the page update and the one-line report gives the page of its landed changes, the report and the reversal. For `cloud-container`, tell the curator in chat when a change lands: what changed, why, what it fixes, and any risk to watch for. If the curator asks, reverse it as that bullet says. So that the curator notices a new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, name it as such at the head of the chat line. - F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled runtime"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). In a hot compiled loop, escape analysis removes the temporary boxes, and one box per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration stays (F-301), as long as C2's inline depth reaches each box's constructor chain (F-302). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4; `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` section 4.

- F-18 **On the compiled path, the class loader makes the class of a generic instantiation at its first use, by rewriting the template's bytecode with ASM, and the rewriting only renames, so it gives no instance a `double[]` field.** The class is `InstantiatingClassloader`; the `fortress-repo` skill's "The compiled runtime" gives the mechanism. A size is part of the made class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, the object `Box` at size 3 in the probe component `pNatMeth`. Inside the class, the size's descriptor is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). A field of the template's type `T`, `LT;`, becomes `LFRR64;` in `Box⟦FRR64⟧`, and `[D` is no class name, so stamping alone keeps every number boxed (F-11). The team's direction for unboxing builds on this class per instantiation (the plan in `compiler/optimization/Unbox.java`; the loader's empty "expando" stub, `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172`), but a loader that stamps an `RR64` instance with a `double[]` field, way A4 of array decision A (P-85), does not exist and is unmeasured. Walk instantiates generics in its own evaluator, not by classes. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1; `coordinator/array-design.md` section 2 (probe 1); `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 3, way A4.
